I would like to share a few insights that I have found with buying brewing equipment from different places around the world. If you are a craft brewer in the US or building a US style craft brewery somewhere else, then this may apply to you.

In the US most craft brewers make beer much like they did since their homebrew days. It is the origin of the modern craft beer scene in America. Single infusion mash with the least amount of equipment possible. Doing it this way has not only help growth it has defined a style that made the US unique. In most other parts of the world beer is a sacred held tradition that is passed down for centuries. Straying from tradition has not been highly regarded. The multi step mash, lager centric styles have dominated the industry for a long time.

So this brings me to equipment. I have purchased equipment made in North America, China, and now Europe. In North America when you get a quote package for a complete brewery you can pretty much just sign the deal. You will get no less, or no more then what you need. Though the prices tend to be much higher than other parts of the world.

In China you can get whatever you ask for. The first quote you get will be for a "complete" brewery. They have certainly confused you with Budweiser. It will have more vessels, packaging equipment, CIP systems, Yeast systems, and many more extras. You need to sit down and thin the quote to only the basics of what you really need. Also I have found it is best to source your own pumps and electronics. Almost all of the companies in China are working off of German designs from decades ago. That does not mean it is bad, you just need to be diligent in asking for exactly what you want, and travel there to do final inspections and changes before it ships.

Europe is a whole other beast. I am currently building a brewery here and I am sourcing all of my equipment here. The largest companies(i.e. the most expensive) have worked with US craft breweries. They know what you want and you can trust them to outfit you perfectly. When you are on a bit of a strict budget you start looking into all the other manufacturers. What I have found is two things. 1. they are going to try to sell you a lager specific system. 2. their prices can be the same as out of china. There are many small brewing manufacturers in Europe that use high quality steel and produce amazing craftsmanship. You just need to hold their hands on what you want. In my situation. Engineers had a difficult time understanding my brewing process. They wanted to combine my boil kettle and mash, separate lauter, and separate whirlpool. When I told them I wanted combo boil/whirlpool, combo mash/lauter they were confused. Some companies just told me they couldn't/wouldn't do it. Others just asked that I meet them in person and go over the design. In those situations I found that you are deleting much of the features they were originally trying to sell you and the price starts looking like China.

So in conclusion, as craft brewers we are almost always looking for the best deals. We are either just starting out or trying to expand, but in most cases money is tight. We look for good quality that we can afford. Some people are very stuck in the Made in the USA, or North America camp. That is fine. Support your home. Some cannot afford that but still want to be in business. I say broaden your horizons. Buying from another country seems scary but with a bit of leg work it can save money and you can get more. Now that I have been doing my research on Europe I say take advantage of the almost equal exchange rate. The quality of work here is amazing and the prices are surprisingly competitive.

I know this might seem strange, but some nights when I go to bed, I have absolutely no recollection of what I dreamed of, or if I dreamed at all. What does this mean?
What's going on in my head when I can't dream?

Our brains aren't rigged up to store dreams in long term memory. You tend to only remember dreams that you wake up from (which would normally be about every 90 minutes), even if you can't remember waking up. Someone please correct me if I'm wrong.

I was going to post the same thing more or less but I could not cite a source so I decided against it. My experience has been that I only remember dreams that get interrupted. That fits with a theory that memory recording is normally disabled during dreaming, and it makes sense that dreams aren't meant to be remembered if you assume human memory is limited.
Not only is there a limited capacity to our memory, but it can sometimes be difficult to remember whether old memories were real or not. Do you get that too?

A good way to remember your dreams more and more is to have a dream journal/diary.

Wake up, write anything down that you can remember. The place, what was going on, who was there, etc.

After a few days, you'll be able to remember most of what's going on. It works. But my dreams are freaking weird :D.
This can apparently help to have more lucid dreams too.

Yes, this + inducing a kind of sleep paralysis.

You trick your body into thinking you're asleep (by not moving one inch at ALL) and sometimes you'll have dreams and you KNOW it's a dream. It was so freaky I stopped trying to do that, but it's possible.
It's ok, ssbtoday. It happens to everyone. Your brain is sleeping. You dream when it wakes up before the rest of you does.

Dreams are basically meant to be forgotten. Generally you dream a few times every time you sleep, but only remember one or two at most. The dream you remember is usually the one you were having right before you woke up (and even that usually fades in a few minutes). You can train yourself to be able to remember your dreams better by keeping a journal that you write your dream down in immediately when you wake up.

I tried this, but I had to quit when I would regularly wake up from a dream and start to write it down only to realize I was in another dream, but now with a notebook. When I would wake up for real, I would only remember the part of the dream involving trying to write down the previous dream in a notebook. This is not a joke; this really happened to me on a regular basis for over a year. It still happens 2-3 times a year. Sometimes I've even had two different notebook dreams.
From what I understand, multiple levels like that is actually pretty common. It can really screw with your head, too.

How The System Works

Artists and people willing to make some art for others leave comments saying how many requests they want to fulfill. Requesters may then respond to the artists and leave a request of their tulpa/wonderland. Finally, the artist can make the requested art and not feel overwhelmed, as they will only be doing as many requests as they stated they wanted to do. This will allow for most or all requests to be fulfilled.

Rules For The Artists

Please state how many pieces of art or requests you are willing to take on. (Only state how many requests you really want to take on. Don't say you'll take 3 requests and end up only fulfilling 1 or 2).

Explain to all users the medium of your art. This can range anywhere from simple #2 pencil on notebook paper, all the way to detailed computer art.

If you choose to, you may include pieces or pics of your previous art to show and demonstrate what your art-style is like.

Rules For The Requesters

Please include details of your tulpa/wonderland that you wish the artist will include in the art (this can include reference pics if you so wish)

Don't hassle the artists and try to get them to rush your request. If you want the art to look good, give them some time.

Refrain from requesting more art from the artists than they stated they are willing to make.

Both artists and requesters: Follow the format and guidelines below.

Format For The Artists

Number of requests willing to take: (State how many requests you wish to take and fulfill) Ex: "I am willing to take 2 requests."

Medium of your art: (State the medium of your art) Ex: "Most of my art is done with pencil on sketch paper, and some pieces are done digitally on my computer."

Format For The Requesters

Type of Request: (state whether your request is a tulpa or a wonderland)

References, if any: (list any references you have, including pics or real life examples)

Description: (include a description of your tulpa/wonderland) For tulpa: list any physical features of your tulpa or any personality traits that you think the artist should include in the art piece. For wonderlands: describe a particular area in your wonderland, include descriptions of it's landscape and such.

Include any extra details: (include any extra comments you have, or anything special you have in mind.)
